title: FRM Part I
tagline: Risk you can measure. Models you can explain.
summary: One-to-one FRM Part I coaching built around GARP practice questions, error diagnosis, and risk models you build and test yourself.
audience: Designed for committed FRM Part I candidates who attempt practice questions before each session and want personal guidance on quantitative and valuation topics. Not a passive lecture series, and no pass is guaranteed.
difference:
Formulas you understand, not memorise.
Every risk measure is worked by hand, then built in a spreadsheet or Python, so you know what it says and where it breaks.
duration: 1-on-1 · Abu Dhabi in person or online

method.title: Learn
method.description: Each topic starts with the format that suits the candidate: independent study, tutor-led teaching, or a mix.

method.title: Solve
method.description: GARP practice questions are worked through in session. The candidate explains their reasoning, and the cause of each error is identified: concept, formula, interpretation, calculation, or timing.

method.title: Apply
method.description: Each topic ends with a short practical task, such as a VaR calculation, a hedge, a bond-pricing sheet, or a regression on market data.

method.title: Revise
method.description: Short, spaced reviews revisit earlier topics through recall quizzes, retried errors, and mixed question sets.

modes.title: Self-study
modes.description:
You read the GARP books and attempt the practice questions on your own schedule. Sessions go straight to what you got wrong or guessed: we trace each error to its cause and agree exactly what to fix before the next session.
Best for: candidates who learn well from the books and want sharp feedback, not more lectures.

modes.title: Tutor-led
modes.description:
I teach each topic live from first principles, with worked examples on a shared whiteboard. You then attempt practice questions straight away, while the idea is fresh, and we review your answers together.
Best for: first-time candidates, career switchers, or anyone who finds a topic hard to learn from the text alone.

modes.title: Hybrid
modes.description:
You read first and mark what is unclear. I teach only those parts, then we move to practice questions, so no session time is spent re-explaining what you already understand. You can switch mode topic by topic.
Best for: candidates with some background who want the fastest route through the curriculum.

modules.title: Valuation and Risk Models
modules.summary: Measure market, credit and operational risk, and value the instruments behind it.
modules.coaching: VaR, duration, convexity, option-pricing and credit questions are reviewed. Calculation and model-assumption errors are diagnosed.
modules.practice: Compute parametric, historical and Monte Carlo VaR for a small portfolio and compare the results.
modules.deliverable: VaR and bond-risk worksheet with a stress scenario.

modules.title: Financial Markets and Products
modules.summary: Understand how banks, funds and derivatives markets work, and how each product transfers risk.
modules.coaching: Questions on forwards, futures, swaps, options and hedging are reviewed. Payoff, sign and day-count errors are diagnosed.
modules.practice: Design a futures hedge for a real exposure and measure how well it worked.
modules.deliverable: Hedge design note with payoff charts.

modules.title: Quantitative Analysis
modules.summary: Use probability, regression and time-series tools to model risk.
modules.coaching: Statistics, hypothesis-testing and regression questions are reviewed. Misread output and formula errors are diagnosed.
modules.practice: Estimate volatility and correlation from real price data and test a simple regression.

modules.title: Foundations of Risk Management
modules.summary: Explain how firms govern risk and what went wrong in the classic failures.
modules.coaching: Concept and case questions are attempted first. The reasoning is checked against the framework the question is testing.
modules.practice: Analyse a historical risk failure and map it to the governance lessons it teaches.
modules.deliverable: One-page case study on a risk-management failure.

options.title: Pay by the hour
options.description: Book 1 to 4 hours whenever you need them, at your home in Abu Dhabi or live online. Ideal for a difficult topic or a mock review, with no commitment.

options.title: Monthly coaching
options.description: 30 hours a month, extendable if you need more, so it works out at AED 100 an hour. A flexible schedule built around your exam date, at your home in Abu Dhabi or live online, with your study plan, Classroom quizzes, mocks and progress together in your student portal.

options.title: Revision crash course
options.description: An intensive revision block before your exam window: full mock reviews, timing strategy and drills on your weakest topics. Dates and fee depend on your exam date.

faqs.question: How is this different from a regular FRM course?
faqs.answer: A regular course teaches a fixed lecture plan to a group. This coaching is one-to-one and built around the candidate’s own attempts at practice questions. Each error is traced to its cause, whether concept, formula, interpretation, calculation or timing, and each risk measure is also built in a spreadsheet or Python.

faqs.question: Are sessions in person or online?
faqs.answer: Both. Sessions are held in person in Abu Dhabi, or live online for candidates in Dubai, elsewhere in the UAE and abroad. Online sessions use a shared screen and whiteboard, so the question work is the same either way. The format can be mixed from week to week.

faqs.question: Is the GARP curriculum still needed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Registered candidates receive the official FRM books and practice questions from GARP. Sessions are built around that material, not around separate notes. Finance in Practice is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by GARP.

faqs.question: Do I need to know Python?
faqs.answer: No. Every topic can be done by hand and in a spreadsheet. Python is offered for candidates who want it, and it is never required for the exam.

faqs.question: Can coaching start at any time, and how are sessions priced?
faqs.answer: Yes, coaching can start at any time, with no fixed cohort date. There are three ways to pay: by the hour (AED 150), monthly (AED 3,000 for 30 hours, extendable, on a flexible schedule at your home in Abu Dhabi or online), or a revision crash course before the exam, priced on request. Every option starts with the free 30-minute diagnostic.

faqs.question: Does coaching guarantee a pass?
faqs.answer: No. Results depend on the candidate’s preparation and effort. Coaching improves the quality of practice by finding the cause of each error and a clear next step.
